Let $D$ be the region enclosed by the curve $C$ parametrized as
$r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ].$ 
The area of $D$ can be written as

$$
\text{Area}(D)={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})dA={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\boxed{}\,dt,
$$

where $P(x,y)=-y$ and $Q(x,y)=0.$ Determine the missing part of the equation.

*Hint: Note that $C$ is negatively oriented.*

current_example.problem:
Let $D$ be the region enclosed by the curve $C$ parametrized as
$\mathbf{r}(t) = \langle 2\sin t, \: 2 \cos t \rangle$ for $t \in \left [0, 2\pi \right).$ 
The area of $D$ can be written as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14247150/assets/d9d4cf88d01c745b95456e954faaf090e6fa8d0c9b3811c2fbe176854f876665.svg)

where $P(x,y) = -y$ and $Q(x,y) = 0.$ Determine the missing part of the equation.

*Hint: Note that $C$ is negatively oriented.*

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14247150/assets/a5eeb5db90f9ee0d86a49e5bbf02629c7886fa019db7cff3c4d0e1eb43e8fd75.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
Our simple, smooth, closed path $C$ is negatively oriented, and  

$$
\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 0 - \left(-1\right) = 1.
$$

So, according to Green's theorem, we can write the area of the region $D$ enclosed by the curve $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(D) & ={∬}_{D}\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

  

Notice that we have to take the line integral with a minus sign since the path is negatively oriented.

Substituting $P(x,y) = -y$ and $Q(x,y) = 0,$ we get

$$
- \oint\limits_C P \: \text{d}x + Q \: \text{d}y = \oint\limits_C y \: \text{d}x.
$$

 

The derivative of $\mathbf r(t)$ is

$$
\mathbf{r}'(t) = \left\langle  2\cos t ,\:  -2 \sin t \right\rangle.
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }4{cos}^{2}⁡t\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the missing expression is $4\cos^2 t.$
